Description

IQGAP1 is a large scaffold that holds the kinases of the cascade at the EGF receptor. It binds ERK2 directly, whether or not cells are stimulated [1]. It binds MEK1 and MEK2 as well. EGF raises its binding to MEK1 and lowers its binding to MEK2, and ERK2 raises the binding of MEK2 fourfold [2]. IQGAP1 also binds BRAF and raises its activity, and without IQGAP1, or with a mutant that cannot bind BRAF, EGF no longer activates BRAF [3]. Through its IQ domain IQGAP1 binds the kinase domain of the EGF receptor, a contact that calmodulin disrupts, and cells lacking IQGAP1 phosphorylate the receptor poorly after EGF [4]. The amount of scaffold matters: both too little and too much IQGAP1 lower the activation of MEK and ERK [1, 2]. A peptide that separates IQGAP1 from ERK blocks tumours driven by RAS and RAF in mice [5].
